transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Rafael Ortega (Equinox Head of ML), Priya Nair (Equinox Infra), Sam Li (Equinox PM)

Summary:
- Quick readout of latest lab bench versus Equinox's incumbent (CloudMesh/NimbusAI) focusing on latency (p50/p95) and throughput.
- Discussed routing playbook, dedicated slot sizing, KV/prefix cache behavior and quantization tradeoffs.
- Agreed on logs + traffic sample handoff and stress test plan.

Topics:
- Raw latency numbers (p50/p95) on 256-token generations
- Throughput (requests/sec and tokens/sec) under simulated traffic mix
- Variance during cold-start and cache-miss scenarios
- Cost per 1M tokens and break-even runway vs incumbent
Action items recap at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda — Maya will run through the bench numbers, then we'll compare to the baseline, then next steps. Rafael, you still see the screen?
[00:12] Rafael Ortega: Yep, yep, all good. thanks Jordan.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Okay so first slide, this is the lab sprint 6 run — scenario was 256-token generation, mixed prompt lengths, 70% single-turn, 30% multi-turn. We used the same dataset you shared, Rafael, minus PII.
[00:30] Priya Nair: small note, the sample had a couple longer contexts than prod, we trimmed but keep that in mind.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Good call. The baseline numbers from CloudMesh (the incumbent you had) were p50 120ms, p95 430ms for that workload in your earlier runs. Our hosted config gave p50 ~38ms, p95 ~180ms. On Dedicated (4xA100, optimized kernels + quantize-8) we saw p50 32ms, p95 135ms.
[00:56] Sam Li: Sorry can you repeat the p95 on dedicated? sounded like 135?
[01:00] Maya Chen: Yeah 135ms p95, that's with our KV prefix caching enabled and batching tuned for 80ms latency headroom.
[01:08] Rafael Ortega: wow that's a big delta from 430 to 135. feels almost too good. what's the throughput numbers at that config?
[01:15] Maya Chen: Right — throughput for the dedicated set was about 620 requests/sec sustained with 300 tokens average produced per request measured as tokens/sec ~186k. Baseline sustained ~340 rps under the same synthetic mix.
[01:29] Priya Nair: how are you measuring concurrent requests? our earlier baseline run was 64 concurrent workers, 256 tokens per request, 2s think time.
[01:38] Maya Chen: We mirrored that: 64 concurrency, same think time. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching so effective kernel utilization is higher; we also warm KV caches between prompts so many cache hits avoided full KV recompute.
[01:51] Rafael Ortega: what's the cold-start behavior? one of our concerns is tail latency when a new model variant spins up.
[01:56] Maya Chen: cold-start p95 jumps to ~420ms for the first 30s under scale up but then stabilizes to 140ms once caches are populated and concurrent steady state is reached. We flagged that — we have a warm standby policy to reduce that delta.
[02:12] Jordan Patel: to add, our fallback routing can send to a cheaper-but-slower model if there's sustained shortage, so you won't see total failure — it's graceful degradation.
[02:21] Sam Li: cost — what's the per-token cost at this dedicated setup vs their reported costs?
[02:26] Maya Chen: rough numbers: for the dedicated run we estimate $0.18 per 1k tokens (after amortizing reserved capacity), baseline reports were closer to $0.32 per 1k tokens for same generation profile. Those are preliminary — Jordan will share a cleaned spreadsheet.
[02:40] Rafael Ortega: are we comparing apples to apples on quantization? baseline was their 8-bit quant, we ran Redwood with int8 plus kernel fusion — any quality difference observed?
[02:49] Maya Chen: We ran automatic quality checks against your eval set — top-1 accuracy delta was <0.7% and hallucination metric diff within noise. So quantize-8 with our kernel path looked comparable.
[02:59] Priya Nair: any differences around multi-turn KV cache—like when the conversation grows to 4–6 turns? baseline had p95 go up a lot in that case.
[03:08] Maya Chen: Good question — we tested up to 8-turns. p95 increases by ~40–60ms compared to single-turn on dedicated; baseline showed jump of 180–220ms. So the relative advantage remains.
[03:20] Rafael Ortega: can you explain batching tradeoffs? sometimes we see batching reduce latency at high qps but increases p50 in lower qps patterns.
[03:28] Maya Chen: Right — continuous batching adapts batch window based on inflight QPS and headroom. For small-scale traffic we keep batch windows tight to avoid adding batch-induced queuing. But for high QPS we expand batches to improve GPU throughput. We tuned thresholds for your traffic mix.
[03:42] Jordan Patel: one thing we observed — when we disabled prefix-cache for a run, p95 climbed to 320ms which is closer to baseline. So cache is doing heavy lifting.
[03:52] Priya Nair: curious about memory and eviction — how stable is KV cache eviction under peak? we had out-of-memory events on CloudMesh during spikes.
[03:59] Maya Chen: eviction is LRU with small TTL for inactive sessions and we offload oversized contexts to RAM-backed slots. In our stress run we saw no OOMs; peak GPU mem at ~87% for 4xA100. We'll attach the mem histograms.
[04:12] Rafael Ortega: okay, the numbers look promising. what about degraded quality edge cases — any examples where baseline produced more relevant answers?
[04:20] Maya Chen: In a handful of prompts with very long code blocks, we saw Redwood returning slightly shorter continuations — probably conservative stopping rules at our batching cutoff. We can tweak generation config; we haven't observed major quality regressions.
[04:33] Sam Li: any security notes? our legal asked about KMS and audit logs.
[04:37] Jordan Patel: yep we have SOC2 in place for hosted; for Private we support customer-managed KMS and audit logs with retention controls. Maya will send the security doc link.
[04:47] Priya Nair: latency during decomm/scale-down — how long to drain in-flight requests?
[04:53] Maya Chen: drain policy is 45s by default, we can extend if you need smoother handoff; at 45s we didn't see tail bursts.
[04:59] Rafael Ortega: quick bench question — you said 620 rps. what's the 99th?
[05:03] Maya Chen: 99th was ~240ms on the dedicated config; baseline 99th ~680ms.
[05:10] Priya Nair: nice. Are these figures reproducible in our VPC private deployment or only in Redwood lab?
[05:16] Maya Chen: we ran identical infra in Private with same model builds and got within 5–8% of these numbers. The biggest lift is network egress/ingress differences in your VPC — which we'll measure once you hand over the trace.
[05:30] Jordan Patel: Rafael, what's your internal target SLA? is p95 <200ms a must or a nice-to-have?
[05:36] Rafael Ortega: strategic target is p95 <250ms for interactive features; ideal is <150ms. so your dedicated 135ms is within ideal which is great.
[05:45] Sam Li: Given the numbers, what's the ask for Dedicated? any special reservation?
[05:49] Maya Chen: For the pilot, we'd recommend a 4-GPU reserved slice for steady-state with autoscale bursts to 8 GPUs for peak windows. That gives headroom and keeps unit cost attractive.
[06:00] Priya Nair: will that require new networking setup? VPC peering?
[06:03] Jordan Patel: For Private, yes peering & direct connect recommended; for hosted we can set IP allowlists and customer-managed keys if you prefer hybrid.
[06:12] Rafael Ortega: okay let's go over the remaining risks quickly. Priya brought up OOM — looks covered. Cold-start — you have warm standby. Security — docs requested. Any other blockers?
[06:22] Sam Li: procurement wanted a rough commercial for scaling — like committed monthly spend.
[06:27] Jordan Patel: we'll include pricing options in the cost spreadsheet — pay-as-you-go vs reserved. Expect that with the playbook.
[06:33] Maya Chen: small note — we patched a kernel regression mid-sprint and re-ran those failing workloads; that's why some earlier lab numbers were noisy. We re-ran with the latest runtime.
[06:44] Rafael Ortega: got it. can you attach the raw histograms and the exact curl commands for reproducing?
[06:48] Maya Chen: yes, will include them in the artifact bundle.
[06:51] Jordan Patel: cool. next steps then — Jordan will send playbook + cost, Maya will upload logs and run the stress, Equinox will send the trace. schedule follow-up for next Wednesday?
[07:03] Rafael Ortega: next Wed works for us. Rafael sign-off on next steps.
[07:07] Sam Li: thanks everyone.
[07:09] Priya Nair: thanks.
